data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 demands a distribution-shift generalization test as the mechanism to distinguish genuine structural alignment from incidental correlation. But for tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, the single evaluation can identify a genuine reliability gain by comparing the panel's performance against the expert's oracle-graded outcomes on held-out cases at the decision boundary. A causal-mechanism stance must explain *why* the panel gets the right answer; SRC_001's proposed shift test only shows that the panel fails under distribution shift, which does not identify the mechanism producing reliability in-distribution. Without identifying the within-distribution causal mechanism (e.g., does the checklist track outcome-discriminative features used by the true generative process?), the shift test alone cannot distinguish genuine reliability gain from mere compliance that happens to track the right answer within the evaluated distribution.
